text:
miguel: Quick async ask — can someone run a tinyburst throughput sweep for continuous-batching tuning? Need a few runs to compare max_batch_tokens and queue_window effects. Short checklist below, no real-time meeting.
sophia: I can take this tonight. Which model / seq len do you want me to use?
miguel: Thanks. Use `redwood/opt-1.3b-quant` (the quantized variant we recently added), seq_len=1024, seed=42. Target configs:
- max_batch_tokens: [2048, 4096]
- queue_window_ms: [5, 15, 30]
- enable_prefix_cache: [true, false]
- run tinyburst profile (1m warmup + 3m steady), collect per-token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, batch size distribution and dropped requests.
Include a small loadgen command you can copy/paste (example):
```bash
./loadgen --model opt-1.3b-quant \
  --seq-len 1024 \
  --concurrency 16 \
  --duration 240 \
  --warmup 60 \
  --max-batch-tokens ${BATCH} \
  --queue-window-ms ${WINDOW} \
  --prefix-cache ${CACHE} \
  --report /tmp/cb-sweep-${BATCH}-${WINDOW}-${CACHE}.json
```
sophia: Got it. I'll run the matrix tonight on staging-gpu-3. Will post artifacts to the perf bucket and a quick summary in the morning. Anything else to capture?
devon: Please also capture `batch_size_histogram` and `kv_cache_hit_rate` if possible. And set `loadgen` to log per-request queue wait times (`--verbose-queue`).
miguel: Perfect. SLO we're trying to keep: median token throughput >= 1500 tok/s per GPU and p99 latency < 120ms for the steady window. If any config violates p99 by >20% vs baseline, flag it as a regression.
sophia: One quick question — for the `enable_prefix_cache=true` runs, do you want TTL tuned? Default is 60s.
devon: For tinyburst, set `cache_ttl=30` so we see eviction effects during the 3m steady. Add a second run with 60s if you have spare cycles.
sophia: Cool. Scheduling now. I'll create a run ticket and link it here.
cb-bot: run-scheduler: Created sweep job `cb-tinyburst-sweep-3398765432` on staging-gpu-3 with 12 tasks. ETA ~2 hours. Logs will be at https://internal.perf/runs/cb-tinyburst-sweep-3398765432
sophia: First pass results (quick summary):
- `max_batch_tokens=2048, queue_window=5ms, cache=false` => med 1420 tok/s, p99 165ms, batch median 3
- `max_batch_tokens=2048, queue_window=15ms, cache=true` => med 1580 tok/s, p99 125ms, batch median 5, kv_hit 0.42
- `max_batch_tokens=4096, queue_window=15ms, cache=true` => med 1700 tok/s, p99 138ms, batch median 7, kv_hit 0.55
- `max_batch_tokens=4096, queue_window=30ms, cache=true` => med 1685 tok/s, p99 160ms, noticed queue tail spikes at ~10% of requests
Attached the perf JSONs: gs://redwood-perf/cb/3398765432/*.json and a short grafana snapshot: https://grafana.internal/d/cb/3398765432
devon: Nice, thanks. Observations:
- 4096 helps median throughput but increases p99 in the 30ms window (queue tailing). Might be queue-window jitter causing long waits for small requests.
- 2048+cache looks like a sweet spot for p99 vs throughput tradeoff.
miguel: Great diagnostics — could you add a short diff against last week's baseline in the run ticket? PR #3421 changes the scheduler heuristics; pinging for a quick perf review.
sophia: Will add perf_diff and tag `perf_regress` if any run crosses the 20% threshold. Also posted a short flamegraph for the 4096/30ms run.
devon: @miguel — quick code-review ping on #3421 (cb scheduler changes). Diffs touch `scheduler.py` around `select_batch` heuristics. Tested locally but want an extra :eyes: on corner cases (late-arrivals & preemption).
miguel: ACK, I'll review before EOD and leave comments. If it's safe, merge with `--no-ff` and add `canary=true` on the rollout.
sophia: Final note for ops: when rolling this to dedicated, use a staged ramp (10% -> 40% -> 100%) and keep `queue_window` at 15ms for the first 24h.
miguel: Thanks everyone. If you hit any flaky runs, drop the raw logs into the ticket and ping `#eng-runtime` with `:rotating_light:`. I'll close the ticket after we have the baseline diff.
devon: Cheers — I'll run an extra 60s-cache TTL job tomorrow morning.
miguel: :thumbsup:
